kurz: Squid has a lot of connective tissue: it turns tender if cooked very briefly or for a long time. In between it is as tough as rubber.
bild_im_kopf: Like a rope bridge across a valley: you either stay right at the near edge or go all the way across. In the middle you get stuck.
faustregeln: For tender squid: either lightning fast or patient, never in between.
If it has already turned tough, keep [[schmoren|braising]] rather than giving up: after half an hour it softens again.

ursachen.titel: Medium cooking time: too long for quick, too short for slow
ursachen.warum: After about two minutes the connective tissue contracts hard. Only after half an hour or more does it turn into soft gelatine (as a guide).
fix: Quick: one or two minutes at most over high heat
Slow: braise gently for at least 30 to 45 minutes, octopus often longer

ursachen.titel: Pan too full or not hot enough
ursachen.warum: Squid releases a lot of water. In a cool pan it boils in its own juice and takes too long to colour.
fix: Fry in small batches in a very hot pan

ursachen.warum: Thick tubes take longer to heat through and so slip into the tough middle zone.
fix: Cut the tubes open and score them in a diamond pattern
Cut into thin rings or strips

q1.frage: Was it in the heat for less than two minutes or more than half an hour?

q2.frage: Was it fried briefly but did the pan barely sizzle?
